# @ouro.bot/shepherd

Shepherd keeps the GitHub Copilot app's sessions as work. Plain ESM, no build step, no runtime dependencies, Node 22.18 or newer.

## Library

- `import { deps, snapshot, sendTo, archive, exchange, appReady } from '@ouro.bot/shepherd'`
- `deps({ copilotHome })` returns `{ now, sleep, sql, history, historySize, exchange }`. `sql` is a read-only query of `<copilotHome>/data.db`.
- `snapshot(deps, now?, skip?)` returns one object per local, unarchived session: `id`, `title`, `mode`, `state` (`busy` or `idle`), `why`, `running`, `interrupted`, `workspaceId`. Sessions over 500 MB, or idle for over 24 h, are `idle` with a `why`.
- `sendTo(deps, id, prompt, waitMs)` returns `{ ok, reply, error }`. It restores a compressed history first, best effort; a restore that can't run never stops the send.
- `archive(deps, row, { keepWorktree, waitMs, compress })` archives `row.workspaceId` as a workspace, deleting its worktree only when `row.workspaceType === 'worktree'` and `keepWorktree` is not set. Without a workspace it archives the session. Returns `{ ok, session_id, error, compressed }`.
- `compressHistory(deps, id, { dryRun })` gzips an archived (or unlisted) session's `events.jsonl` to `events.jsonl.gz` and returns `{ id, ok, before, after, why }`. It refuses a live session, a file a process has open, and an existing `.gz`. Each compression appends a `history-compressed` row to the disk ledger.
- `restoreHistory(deps, id)` gunzips a compressed history back and returns `{ id, ok, restored, why }`.
- `exchange(copilotHome, messages, { done, keep, waitMs })` and `appReady(deps)` talk to the app's socket on `<copilotHome>/run/ws.port` and `ws.token`.
- `resume(deps, { targets, startedAt, restartedAt, why, lanes, t, log })` sends each target one resume message and waits for a turn; `targets` comes from `pickTargets({ before, after, also })`, `resumeText({ at, why, lanes })` is the message. `RESUME_T` holds the default timings: `grace` (the caller's wait before its snapshot), `delivery`, `retry`, `tries`, `concurrency`, `backoff`. A history over 500 MB is held through `deps.heldBack`, never sent. When anything resumed it writes `<state>/resume-last.json`.
- `loopState(lines)`, `lastTurnAt(lines)`, `continuedSince(lines, since)`, `tookTurnSince(lines, since)`, `lastReply(lines, since)`, `readTail(file, bytes?)`, and the `READY` and `DEFER` tokens read a session's history.
- Errors are `ShepherdError` with `code`, `problem` and `fix`; the message reads `<problem>. Fix: <fix>.`

## CLI

- `shepherd status [--json] [--copilot-home <dir>]`: one line per local session.
- `shepherd restore-history <id> [--json]`: puts back an archived session's compressed history, for a session unarchived by hand.
- `shepherd watch [--quiet] [--json]`: one pass of the six-hour health watch over the resumed sessions (roster from `<state>/resume-last.json`, state in `<state>/health-watch.json`), then exit. A session that stays broken is reported to the agent with `ouro msg`.
- `shepherd watch --status [--json]`: what the health watch is following: healthy, waiting, asked again, broken.
- `shepherd install [--dry-run]`: loads `~/Library/LaunchAgents/bot.ouro.shepherd.plist`, which runs `shepherd watch --quiet` every 60 s. `--dry-run` prints the plist and changes nothing.
- `shepherd help`.
- Run it without installing: `npx github:ourostack/shepherd#v0.3.0 status --json` (not on npm yet).
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the app's data could not be read, the history could not be restored, or the agent could not load, 2 usage. Errors are one line.

## Rules

- Shepherd is read-only except `sendTo`, `archive`, `compressHistory`, `restoreHistory`, `resume` (its record in the state folder), `watch` (its state folder and the agent notice) and `install` (the launch agent). It compresses only archived or unlisted sessions, never a live one. It never quits or relaunches the app; that is Housesitter's job.
- Every failure says what probably happened and the fix.
- Tests run against fakes (`test/fake-app.mjs` is a pretend socket). The real database test and CLI status test run only where `/usr/bin/sqlite3` exists.
- Keep it small. A duty moves here only when a caller needs it.
